I've been through ED treatment and recovery many times. Let me tell you that their goal is NOT to get you to an overweight BMI. 70 pound weight loss in 1 year is a LOT and still can cause major damage to your body even if you technically aren't at an underweight BMI. It is accepted in the eating disorder treatment community that BMI is not the end-all-be-all in deciding how severe your eating disorder is.

Your meal plan will be individualized to your individual nutritional needs. It might seem like a lot of food, but when you start eating again you will probably LOSE weight at first. It sounds impossible given CICO but after severe/heavy restriction and weight loss, when introduced to food again your body will go into a hypermetabolism mode as it repairs the damage done to your body.

Your weight might yoyo while it figures out what your healthy set point is. Your treatment team will be following your weight, vital signs, lab tests, and your psychological state to figure out what a healthy weight target is for you. Most likely it will be somewhere between a BMI of 21-23, depending on your age, ethnicity, and weight history (if you are a teenager or early twenties they will probably look at your childhood growth charts to see where you typically fall).

This all sounds very scary right now but I highly encourage you to put your faith in your treatment team. Do not trust the advice of other people here who are not educated in eating disorders and the complicated relationship between physical and mental health it creates.
I also would like to point out people like Jameela Jamil, she's recovered from anorexia and is still in a normal BMI range.
